metadata.case_name: LAM HOK FAI v. CHAN SAI KIT AND ANOTHERS

source: Physical examination revealed laceration over the Plaintiff’s vertex.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

source: Mr Lam was free from psychiatric morbidity before the accident. He suffers from a psychiatric sequela of the accident, i.e., Major Depressive Disorder.

manifestations.description: subjective impairment of cognition and memory
auditory hallucination and persecutory delusion (psychotic features at stage)
slow speech / stammering / difficulty expressing himself
anger, violent behaviour (beat children, slapped wife)
reduced work capacity / inability to work in pre-accident job
feeling frightened about going outside / reduced confidence to go out

treatments_received: Initial hospital admission and discharge the following day for scalp laceration
Admission to Psychiatric Ward (18 June 2002 to 5 July 2002)
Admission to Acute Psychiatric Ward (9 October 2003)
Attendance at Psychiatric Day Hospital (Shatin Hospital) from 11 July 2002 and resumed 4 July 2003
Private psychiatric treatment with Dr Law Wun Tong (September 2003; 5 consultations)
Occupational therapy and Day Hospital rehabilitation
Medications including Amitriptyline, Fluoxetine, Ativan, Dologesic, Deanxit, Stemetil, Nortriptyline, Lithium, Stelazine
treatments_future: Intensive cognitive psychological therapy / intensive psychotherapy (recommended 15-20 sessions or course of 9 months to 2 years)
Continue psychiatric medication and Day Hospital rehabilitation
Out-patient neurological check-ups and psychotherapy/family therapy

losses.description: Marital and family breakdown: wife deserted him in August 2001; separation and impact on relationship with two children
Became dull, reticent and quiet; spoke slowly; lost temper easily; became irritable and violent (beat his children, slapped his wife)

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: His sex life with his wife was very much affected
Impaired concentration and subjective impairment of cognition and memory

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Felt frightened about going outside and had vague ideas of being followed by unknown people
Unable to return to pre-accident construction site job; likely unable to hold open employment; 100% loss of earning capacity (as assessed by Dr Wong and accepted in part by the Court)
